title: Streamline catalog intake: tagging taxonomy, shadow-pinning, and enterprise eval gate workflow
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Replace ad-hoc model onboarding requests with a deterministic intake and triage flow that balances enterprise needs (pinning/deprecation) with service-level economics and safety. This ticket implements three tightly-coupled pieces: a) a compact tagging taxonomy and automated heuristics that surface enterprise-relevant attributes at intake, b) a 'shadow-pin' workflow that allows enterprise customers to request version pinning while traffic is mirrored to the pinned model for evaluation before full pin enforcement, and c) an eval-gating checklist and automation to ensure we don't regress downstream customers when adding new models or pins.

Scope and rationale: Enterprise customers frequently ask for immediate version pinning to guarantee output stability; operations and infra teams are concerned about sudden load and quality regressions. The current intake lacks consistent metadata (SLOs, token-cost sensitivity, eval set) making prioritization noisy. Shadow-pin provides a safe middle ground: the model is pinned in routing tables for policy and metering purposes but traffic is mirrored (no go/no-go) during an observation window. If metrics are within thresholds, the pin flips to active traffic routing. This reduces emergency rollback churn and preserves predictability for other customers.

Deliverables: 
- Intake form fields (+ SDK and UI): expected QPS, acceptable tail latency, token-cost sensitivity, required compliance region, suggested eval set (link), and an enterprise impact flag.
- Tagging taxonomy and heuristics service: automated tags applied at intake (e.g., enterprise_contract, compliance_region, latency_sensitive, cost_sensitive, offline_eval_requested). Rules and confidence explained in UI.
- Shadow-pin controller: orchestration that creates a mirrored routing policy + observation window (configurable per request). Controller integrates with routing, telemetry, rollout APIs.
- Eval-gate automation: per-pin eval runner that runs customer-specified eval set or a default benchmark, collects metrics (quality deltas, hallucination rate, latency percentiles, token cost delta), and evaluates against thresholds.
- Console UX: new table in Model Catalog showing shadow-pinned requests, observation status, pass/fail signal, runbook links, and a single-click promote/rollback.
- Telemetry and dashboards: Grafana panels for shadow-pins, regression alerts, cost delta, and per-customer impact estimator.
- Documentation and runbooks: intake owner guide, on-call playbook for pin failures, and SLO update notes for Dedicated/Private tenants.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Open decisions / trade-offs: 
- Default observation window length: proposed 48 hours vs. 7 days for high-risk customers. 48h reduces time-to-stability but may miss rare regressions; proposal: 48h default with configurable escalation to 7d for high-risk labels.
- Mirroring overhead: mirrored requests double runtime cost during observation. We need infra guardrails (budget limit, opt-out) for customers with tight cost constraints.
- Eval standardization: accept either customer-provided eval sets or our default curated suite. For enterprise contracts require a sponsor-approved eval set.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Shadow-pin masks production training drift because mirrored traffic is not identical to live routing (cookie differences, auth). Mitigation: log enriched request context and run a small % of real traffic through the pinned model in early hours for sanity checks.
- Risk: Too many pending shadow-pins create operational state. Mitigation: enforce expiration policy and auto-archive after 14 days unless extended.

Rollout plan (high-level): 
1) Build intake form + tagging heuristics + admin UI (2 sprints)
2) Implement shadow-pin controller + basic mirror routing (1 sprint)
3) Hook eval-gate automation with default eval suite and dashboards (1 sprint)
4) Pilot with 3 enterprise customers (2 weeks each) and iterate thresholds
5) GA with docs and runbooks, add guardrails for cost and expiration

Stakeholders and owners: 
- PM owner: Asha Patel (this ticket)
- Eng leads: Liam O'Connor (routing/controller), Maya Chen (telemetry), Diego Ramirez (console)
- Security/compliance: Priya Shah (review for customer data in evals)
- Solutions Eng: Miguel Torres (pilot coordination)

Operational notes: 
- Every shadow-pin will create a ticket in the 'catalog-ops' queue and surface an email to the assigned owner.
- Shadow-pins must emit a standardized event to event-bus with fields: request_id, customer_id, model_family, pin_version, start_ts, window_hours, eval_result_summary.

Future work (outside scope): automated cost allocation per mirror, opt-in for sampling rather than full mirror, integration with canary A/B framework for multi-model rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form with required enterprise metadata is available in Console and SDK and validated against schema
Automated tagging service applies enterprise-relevant tags with confidence scores and these are visible in the catalog list
Shadow-pin controller can create a mirrored routing policy and set a configurable observation window; mirror traffic is recorded and costs are metered
Eval-gate automation runs scheduled tests against the pinned variant and produces pass/fail with metrics (quality delta, latency P95, token cost delta)
Console shows shadow-pin status and allows promote/rollback; promote flips routing to the pinned model according to policy
Grafana dashboards present shadow-pin metrics and alerts trigger on regression thresholds
Pilot with at least three enterprise customers completed and pilot feedback documented in linked Confluence page
